newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court finds Greece late to implement plant protection laws.
newsitem.headline: Court finds Greece late to implement plant protection laws.

text.p: The European Court of Justice ruled on Thursday that Greece had not implemented EU rules on plant protection within the time frame prescribed by the directive.

Greece did not deny that the directive had not been transposed within the time allowed, but stated that a draft presidential decree had been drawn up by the Ministry of Agriculture. After finalisation, the decree is scheduled to be submitted to the Council of State and then to the President of the Republic for signature.
The court said that since the directive had not been transposed, the Commission's action was well-founded.
(Court translation into English. Original language of the case: Greek)
"Failure by a member state to fulfil its obligations - Directive 91/414/EEC - Failure to transpose"

application for a declaration that, by failing to adopt within the prescribed period the laws, regulations or administrative provisions necessary to comply with Council directive 91/414/EEC of 15 July 1991 concerning the placing of plant protection products on the market, the Hellenic Republic has failed to fulfil its obligations under the EC Treaty and that directive

1. Declares that, by failing to adopt within the prescribed period the laws, regulations or administrative provisions necessary to comply with Council directive 91/414/EEC of 15 July 1991 concerning the placing of plant protection products on the market, the Hellenic Republic has failed to fulfil its obligations under article 23 of that directive;
2. Orders the Hellenic Republic to pay the costs.
